summary.intent: Get PR #546 (feat/version-checkpoint-resume) to zero open findings in Entire by fixing or addressing each review finding, including a new Medium finding about npm platform-owner optional-dependency pin writes breaking checkpoint resume.
summary.outcome: Earlier in the session, the GIT_DIR and workspace-membership findings were fixed, committed (7378f3148, signed), resolved in Entire, and pushed. For the new npm platform-owner finding, the claim was checked against apply.rs and the limit was recorded in ADR 0013's consequences (the first edit missed and was redone), doc-check was run, and a docs commit was made; the finding dismissal and push were not yet shown as done.

repo: Workflow order the user wants for review findings: fix and verify locally, commit (signed with -S), resolve findings in Entire with notes pointing at the commit, then push.
Entire findings are queried with `entire trail finding --repo gh/orin-dx/callisto --branch <branch> --freshness any [--status open] --json`, which returns counts and a findings list.
`just pre-push`, `just lint`, `just doc-check`, clippy and full workspace tests are the pre-push checks; `just doc-check` covers ADR docs.

Architectural decisions for the version checkpoint/resume feature live in docs/adr/0013-interrupted-version-runs-resume-from-a-checkpoint-ref.md, and known limits are recorded in its Consequences section.
The `version` command now records no checkpoint when GIT_DIR, GIT_WORK_TREE or GIT_INDEX_FILE is set, because the scratch checkout's `git reset` could otherwise act on the user's real repository.

code.finding: The resume guard compares the run output hash with the checkpoint and the completed scratch tree, and refuses with E340 otherwise. This misfires for npm platform owners interrupted between the version write and the pin writes.
Planning schedules optional-dependency pin updates for npm platform owners as separate writes from the owner's own version.
Apply persists the npm platform owner's version and pins as separate writes (see also lines 469-472), leaving a non-atomic intermediate state.

workflow: Verify a review finding against the code before acting on it.
When a finding is accepted as a limitation instead of fixed, record it in the ADR first as the durable record, then dismiss the finding with a note that points at it.
Confirm each regression test fails without its fix.
An Edit that misses its target changes nothing, so a following commit step can find no changes. Grep for the exact wording before retrying.

friction: The first ADR Edit failed to match, so the first commit attempt had nothing to commit and the exact wording had to be grepped and the edit redone.
Entire's review runs asynchronously after each push, so new findings keep arriving after the count reaches zero.
The user has to do CI approval, the Entire Gates approval, and the merge themselves.
